dialogue.content: I'll have 12 unused PTO days at the end of 2026. How many of them do I lose, and is there a deadline for using the ones I keep?

With 12 unused PTO days at the end of 2026, you'd lose **2 days** and keep **10 days**.

The current rule (from the People Operations announcement posted 2025-11-17, which replaced Section 5 of the PTO Policy and the matching handbook section) allows you to carry over up to **10 days (80 hours)** of unused PTO into the next calendar year. Anything above that limit is forfeited on December 31 — except where state law doesn't permit forfeiture, so check your state if that might apply.

**Deadline for the days you keep:** carried-over PTO must be used by **June 30** of the year you carry it into — so your 10 carried days would need to be used by June 30, 2027.

Note that older documents (the PTO Policy HR-101 and the Employee Handbook) still say 5 days and a March 31 deadline; the November 2025 announcement explicitly supersedes those, and the policy document will be reissued at its next annual review.
